releases.name: v0.14.9 — Optional Ko-fi support
releases.body:
# v0.14.9 — Optional Ko-fi support

- Integrate #304's `ko_fi: zufallupon` repository funding entry while preserving GitHub Sponsors configuration. Add the matching Ko-fi link to the README with explicit English/Japanese statements that support is entirely optional. No feature access, paid benefit or preferential treatment is promised.
- Publish that updated README in the npm archive; `.github/FUNDING.yml` takes effect on GitHub's default branch, not as an npm runtime setting. GitHub Sponsors approval/publication remains separate from this repository change.
- Align current README/OpenCode/Codex/Japanese/Chinese guide pins with v0.14.9, preserving historical releases and measured-results details. No execution behavior, dependency, permission or model-default change.

## Review and validation

Before #304 integration, collect its body, ordinary comments, review bodies and inline comments. Two automatic review failure/usage-limit notices are deferred external review without concrete code findings, not independent PASS. All four exact-head Linux/Windows CI checks succeeded. Retain its recorded document/link/install-example/YAML/target-link checks, then verify integrated funding fields and current release references without replaying setup smoke, external Chat consultations, benchmarks or original product Missions.

Freeze one integrated main commit and tarball/SHA-256 before isolated candidate preflight and one mandatory `npm run test:full`. Verify exact-commit Windows CI and actual native Terra/max Worker startup. Startup smoke establishes only actual Worker/model identity, not Mission completion, independent acceptance or official scoring.

Apply the same archive to both existing npm global prefixes and the OpenCode config-local package, compare packaged files/assets and preserve explicit settings. Publish the fixed tag, GitHub Release and npm `latest` once. Record command/exit/timing, costs, review dispositions and package identity in `_testenv/releases/0.14.9/`. Unrelated PRs appearing during a fixed release are recorded separately rather than failing final accounting or changing the candidate; successful checks/publication are not repeated.

Mission marker: `0.14.9-optional-kofi-v1`. Codex skill marker remains `0.14.6-codex-skill-v1`. Complete OpenCode restart remains manual; installed files do not prove a running host reloaded. Registry propagation is separate from accepted npm publication, with no republish on a temporary 404. No original Mission ledger edits, budget reset/increase or shared-host restart.

- Candidate preflight: passed; eight exact installed runtime assets, OpenCode V2 config/agents and package identity verified; no provider inference requests.
- Linux `npm run test:full`: **2437** passing, **4** explicitly skipped live tests across **133** files, no missing/duplicate scheduled files, exit 0, 387.306 s.
- [Fixed-commit CI](https://github.com/zufall-upon/Sortie-dogs/actions/runs/40655715620): Linux job passed; Windows **55/55**, exit 0.
- Native CLI startup: real Worker `openai/gpt-6.1-terra#max` after 15.339 s; Operator `openai/gpt-6.1-sol#xhigh`; exact fixed-package assets. # v0.14.8 — Host fit, evidence boundaries and current setup

- Publish #302's README guidance on when an existing OpenCode V2 or Codex CLI user benefits from retained goals, direct or delegated implementation, validation/review/correction and evidence-backed handoff. Ordinary questions or small changes that do not need that lifecycle can use the host directly.
- Put the limits of recorded results before the examples: historical fixed-package/model/task runs do not measure the current release/default Worker or establish comparative superiority, guaranteed unattended completion, lower cost or recommendation-rate improvements. Mission acceptance, official scoring and leaderboard acceptance remain separate.
- Publish the package description and `codex`/`codex-cli` keywords already merged in #302. The prior v0.14.7 archive/installed package predates those metadata changes; this release makes them available through a new immutable npm version.

This release updates identity and current guide pins, not execution logic, permissions, model defaults, dependencies or host configuration. No new benchmark, recommendation-rate measurement or replay of prior product Missions.

Apply the same tarball to both existing npm global prefixes and the OpenCode config-local package, compare all packaged files/assets and retain explicit settings. Publish the fixed tag, GitHub Release and npm `latest` once; retain exact command/exit/timing, review, hash and known/unknown-cost receipts in `_testenv/releases/0.14.8/`.

releases.name: v0.14.7 — Visible same-Mission recovery
releases.body:
# v0.14.7 — Visible same-Mission recovery

- Keep `operator_status`, `plan_units`, `cancel_operator` and `submit_mission` reachable when a direct unit's writer activation fails with `manifest-overlap` (#300). Management no longer depends on acquiring the conflicting artifact writer; actual artifact operations and successful completion retain their existing binding and validation checks.
- Hand off only the owner's quiescent direct unit while retaining its Mission, run, unit, reservation, checks and work. In-flight tools/binding prevent handoff, denied releases remain errors, and a live or unproven other owner is not evicted (#300).
- Explain the observed stop, retained results and next action in ordinary conversation. A normal affirmative response can continue authorized recovery without a hidden command, new Mission, budget reset or additional approval gate. Ordinary autonomous recovery still needs no new approval (#300).
- Prepare repository GitHub Sponsors metadata and a README support link; account approval/publication remains separate, not a claim that sponsorships are already active (#299).

## Retained evidence and boundaries

Before #300 integration, the PR body, ordinary comments, review bodies and inline comments were collected. Two automatic review failure/usage-limit notices are deferred external review with no concrete code findings, not independent PASS. Retain the separately reported final-head independent Reviewer PASS/no unresolved Major or Medium, the candidate targeted/full/Windows results and the isolated real-model recovery conversation without repeating inference. Final-head Linux/Windows CI was successful; CI is not finding resolution.

The reported real-model probe used Sol/xhigh and continued the same Mission/run/unit after an ordinary affirmative response, with an actual successful check and Mission receipt. It does not identify the original report's conflicting owner or establish recovery/completion of that original product task. Its estimated $0.2331232 (0 unpriced requests) is separate from the original implementation Mission's unknown cumulative cost.

## Release verification

Freeze one integrated `main` commit and tarball/SHA-256 before isolated candidate preflight and one mandatory `npm run test:full`. Verify exact-commit Windows CI and actual native Terra/max Worker startup. Reuse the retained recovery-specific conversation rather than replaying it merely for release. Startup smoke is not Mission completion, independent acceptance or official task scoring.

Apply the same archive to both existing npm global prefixes and the OpenCode config-local package, compare package files/runtime assets and preserve explicit user settings. Publish the fixed tag, GitHub Release and npm `latest` once; record command/exit/timing, costs and review dispositions under `_testenv/releases/0.14.7/`.

Mission marker: `0.14.7-visible-recovery-v1`. Codex skill marker remains `0.14.6-codex-skill-v1`; its files are unchanged. Attachment handling, ordinary Terra Standard/max defaults, other roles and explicit overrides are unchanged. No original Mission ledger edits, new benchmark or shared-host restart. Complete OpenCode restart remains manual to confirm the already-running host loaded the installed version.

# v0.14.6 — Original attachments, native images and Terra Worker

- Retain original user attachment bytes, message IDs and within-message order through V2 history, compacted/cold Mission continuity, Coordinator/Worker handoff and Operator acceptance (#297). Inline bytes become content-addressed read references; source messages remain unchanged.
- Preserve native image/file tool-result blocks, ordering and metadata when V2 adapts textual reports. Unchanged text leaves the original multimodal result intact, including public `read` and Code Mode results (#297).
- Explain Operator supervision against actual original requirements and evidence. Functional/Review PASS or an honestly unverified caveat does not establish a required visual comparison. Continue authorized mandatory work autonomously while permitting optional caveats, valid alternatives and reused evidence; no universal screenshot duty, pixel-exact matching or new approval gate (#297).
- Default only the ordinary Worker to `openai/gpt-6.1-terra#max`, Standard without Fast/priority. Keep explicit overrides, Scout/dedicated Luna and management/review roles separate. Include Terra API-equivalent token estimates without treating unknown usage as zero or estimating subscription allowance (#297).

# v0.14.5 — Reviewer test organization and unborn Git proof

- Organize Reviewer correction coverage by lifecycle/self-recheck, continuation, scope, validation and permissions (#295). Retain all 209 original cases and all 81 byte-identical registration blocks; add one fixture-isolation regression. Share only plain committed Git inputs, not Mission state, native history, ledgers or plugin instances.
- Serial local observation: 209 cases in 107.027 s before; 210 cases in 101.358 s after (5.669 s / 5.3% lower). This is one before/after observation, not a statistical or full-suite speed claim. The main benefit is focused execution and smaller, purpose-specific files; no test deletion or production cache.
- Observe fresh Git-only Docker workspaces before their first commit (#294). Only an absent symbolic HEAD target permits the repository-format empty-tree comparison. Existing/broken refs and failed observations remain unavailable. No initial commit, Git identity, task dependency installation or object write is required.
